rules.help: Required ARIA attributes must be provided

examples.summary:
Fix any of the following:
  Required ARIA attribute not present: aria-checked

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have inner text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute
  Element does not have an implicit (wrapped) <label>
  Element does not have an explicit <label>
  Element's default semantics were not overridden with role="none" or role="presentation"

findings.title: Target Size (Minimum)
notes: Introduced in WCAG 2.2. Not part of the harmonised EN 301 549 V3.2.1 (2021-03), which adopts WCAG 2.1. Treat as good practice and future-proofing, not as a current EAA obligation.
Expected to become required when EN 301 549 V4.1.1 is cited, scheduled for 2026-11-30. Fixing it now is early, not wasted.

arriving.title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
arriving.why: Requires knowing whether a sticky header or cookie bar covers the focused control at the moment it receives focus.

arriving.title: Dragging Movements
arriving.why: Requires finding every drag interaction and confirming a single-pointer alternative exists.

arriving.title: Target Size (Minimum)
arriving.why: axe-core measures rendered target geometry directly.

arriving.title: Consistent Help
arriving.why: Requires comparing where help appears across several pages, and judging whether it is the same help.

arriving.title: Redundant Entry
arriving.why: Requires walking a multi-step form and noticing information asked for twice.

arriving.title: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
arriving.why: Requires judging whether a login imposes a cognitive function test with no alternative.

leaving.title: Parsing
leaving.why: Removed in WCAG 2.2. Duplicate ids and malformed markup stop being a conformance failure in their own right, though they still cause real problems that other criteria catch.

manualOnly.what: More than one way to locate a page
manualOnly.why: Requires judging whether site search, a sitemap or navigation genuinely offer alternative routes.
Requires comparing repeated components across several pages.
Requires judging whether the same function is named the same way throughout.

manualOnly.what: Error prevention on legal, financial and data entry
manualOnly.why: Requires walking a real checkout or submission flow to confirm it is reversible, checked or confirmed.
Captions, transcripts and audio description have to be watched and read to confirm they are accurate, not merely present.

manualOnly.what: Keyboard operability of the full journey
manualOnly.why: Automation reaches individual controls; only a manual pass proves an entire task can be completed by keyboard alone.
The documentation itself must meet the standard, and it usually lives outside the scanned pages.
Support channels must accommodate users with disabilities. Nothing on the page reveals this.

analysis.coverageNote: Automated testing detects roughly 30 to 40 percent of WCAG failures. A clean automated result is a starting point, not a conformance claim.
